adm.disclaimer: **A help template, not legal advice.** These texts are written from your answers: they are a good starting point, but they do not replace the advice of a qualified person. Read them before you publish, and ask for advice if your situation is unusual (online sales, sensitive data, minors…). You remain responsible for what your site says.
adm.disclaimer.short: **A help template, not legal advice.** Read what you publish.
adm.noPath: This extension has no address on your site, so nothing can be published. Open the “General” tab and give it an address (for example “legal”).
adm.intro.title: Your legal pages in a few minutes
adm.intro.text: I ask you 6 to 8 questions in plain words, then I prepare three pages for you, in French and in English:
adm.intro.notice: **Legal notice**: who publishes the site and who hosts it;
adm.intro.privacy: **Privacy**: what the site collects, why, for how long, and your visitors' rights;
adm.intro.cookies: **Cookies**: what the site puts in the browser, honestly.
adm.intro.how: Nothing is published without your approval: you read a preview first. If an answer is missing, a page is never published half-done: I tell you what is left to fill in.
adm.intro.seen: I have already spotted on your site: **{names}**. I will prefill what goes with it.
adm.justPublished: It is online! Your three pages are available to your visitors.
adm.status.ready: Everything is ready: read the preview, then publish.
adm.status.todo: Some answers are still to be filled in before publishing ({n}).
adm.publish.title: Preview and publication
adm.preview.open: See the preview of my three pages
adm.publish.ack: I have read the texts and I know they are help templates, not legal advice
adm.publish.ackHelp: The three pages will be visible to everyone, in French and in English.
adm.publish.blocked: I cannot publish yet: some answers are still to be filled in or confirmed ({n}). Look for what is marked “To fill in” or “To confirm” in the list.
adm.live.title: What is online
adm.navTip: Tip: by default a “Legal pages” link also appears in the menu at the top of the site. To keep it at the bottom of the page only, untick “Show in my site's menu” in the “General” tab.
adm.live.all: Take the three pages off the site
adm.live.keep: Your answers are kept: you can publish again.
adm.live.confirm: Take the three pages off the site? Your answers are kept: you can publish them again.
adm.collect.unknown: Extensions I do not know: **{names}**. Tell me below whether they collect anything.
adm.preview.title: Preview of your pages
adm.unpublished: Your pages have been taken off the site.
rem.start: Answer the questions to prepare your legal pages.
rem.todo: Your pages are not ready yet: some answers are still to be filled in ({n}).
rem.ready: Your pages are ready: read the preview and publish them.
rem.changed: You changed something since the last publication: publish again to bring the site up to date.
rem.changedTodo: You changed something since the last publication, but some answers are still to be filled in before publishing again ({n}).
rem.added.collector: The extension “{name}” was added since your last publication and it collects information: check what your pages say.
rem.added.unknown: The extension “{name}” is new since your last publication and I do not know it: tell me whether it collects anything.
rem.removed.collector: The extension “{name}” is no longer installed: your pages may still talk about what it collected.
rem.old: Your pages date from {date}. Read them again at least once a year: rules and your site change.
note.mismatch: An extension of your site does collect {what}, yet you answered no. Check the “Information collected” step.
note.thirdParty: Content from another service can set its own cookies and receives your visitors' IP address. In Belgium and France you should in principle ask for their consent before showing it: this template does not add a consent banner. To stay without a banner, replace that content with a simple link.
note.list: An e-mail list needs each person's clear consent, and every message must offer a way to unsubscribe. This template writes it on the page, but it is up to you to follow it.
note.list.CA: In Canada, the anti-spam law requires each person's consent and an unsubscribe link in every message. This template writes it on the page, but it is up to you to follow it.
note.keep: You promise to delete the messages you receive {period} after your last exchange with the person. Remember to clean up your address book.
note.sellsHere: You sell on your site: this template does not write your terms of sale or the information about the right of withdrawal. They have to be written separately.
note.addressVisible: Your address will be visible to everyone. If it is your home, you may prefer not to show it (“Address and phone” step).
st.country.title: Where do you live (or where is your association or company based)?
st.country.help: Rules change from one country to another: this answer decides which details are required and which rights are explained to your visitors. For another country the texts stay general: have them checked carefully.
st.who.title: Who publishes this site?
st.who.help: This is the person or organisation responsible for what the site publishes. This information will be visible to everyone in your legal notice.
st.address.title: How can people reach you?
st.address.help.BE: If your site is linked to an activity, even a small one, Belgian law asks for an address. For a purely personal site, you decide what you show.
st.address.help.FR: In France the law asks for the publisher's name, address and phone number. A private individual (with no professional activity) may keep them private, provided they gave them to their host: tick the first box in that case.
st.address.help.CH: In Switzerland a site that sells or offers services must show the publisher's identity and address. For a personal site, you decide what you show.
st.address.help.CA_QC: In Canada there is no legal notice required for every site, but a contact address reassures your visitors. Give what you are happy to make public.
st.address.help.CA: In Canada there is no legal notice required for every site, but a contact address reassures your visitors. Give what you are happy to make public.
st.address.help.OTHER: Give what you are happy to make public, and check the rules of your country.
st.business.title: What are your official details?
st.business.help.BE: The company number (BCE) must appear on a site linked to an activity.
st.business.help.FR: The SIRET number (or RCS for a company) and the name of the person in charge of publication must appear.
st.business.help.CH: The company identification number (IDE) is expected from registered businesses.
st.business.help.CA_QC: In Quebec, the enterprise number (NEQ) reassures your visitors but is not asked of every organisation.
st.business.help.CA: Give the number that officially identifies your activity, if you have one.
st.business.help.OTHER: Give the number that officially identifies your activity, if you have one.
st.host.title: Who hosts your site?
st.host.help: This is the company that keeps your site's files on its computers. Its name is on your invoice. If you do not know it, leave it empty: that part will not be published.
st.host.help.FR: In France the law asks for the host's name, address and phone number. You find them on its invoice or in its legal notice.
st.collect.title: What do you collect from your visitors?
st.collect.help: Tick everything that applies to your site, even if it is rare. I prefill what I recognise from the installed extensions: read it over, only you know your site.
st.keep.title: How long do you keep the messages?
st.keep.help: After this time you promise to delete the messages you received. Choose a period you will really keep to.
st.sells.title: Do you sell anything?
st.sells.help: This template does not write terms of sale. If you sell, they have to be written separately.
f.country.label: Country
f.status.label: You are
f.name.label: Name
f.name.help: Write it as in your official documents. Example: Jane Martin. In France, a private individual may also use a pseudonym.
f.email.label: Contact e-mail address
f.email.help: Your visitors will be able to write to you here, and it is where they exercise their rights. Prefilled with your site's contact address, if you set one.
f.address.label: Postal address
f.address.help.person: Optional. It will be visible to everyone: if it is your home, think before publishing it.
f.address.help.personFR: Visible to everyone in your legal notice. You prefer not to show it? Leave it empty and tick the two boxes below.
f.address.help.business: Registered office or business address. Example: 12 Lilac Street, 1000 Brussels.
f.hideAddress.label: I am a private individual and I prefer not to show my address
f.hostAck.label: I have given my full identity to my host
f.hostAck.help: Needed to keep your address private: the law requires it. Do it with your host before publishing.
f.phone.label: Phone
f.phone.help.FR: Required by law when you show your identity. Example: +33 1 23 45 67 89.
f.legalForm.label: Legal form
f.legalForm.help: Example: SRL, SAS, ASBL, non-profit association.
f.regNumber.label: Registration number
f.regNumber.help.CA: Optional if you do not have one.
f.regNumber.help.OTHER: Optional if you do not have one.
f.vat.label: VAT number
f.vat.help: Optional: only if you are registered for this tax.
f.capital.label: Share capital
f.director.label: Publication director
f.director.help: The person responsible for what is published. For a self-employed person, that is you.
f.hostName.label: Name of the host
f.hostName.help: Example: the name on your hosting invoice.
f.hostAddress.label: Address of the host
f.hostPhone.label: Phone of the host
f.hostCountry.label: Country where the servers are
f.hostCountry.help: Optional. Useful to explain where your visitors' information goes.
f.collect_messages.label: Private messages (name, e-mail address, message), for example with a contact form
f.collect_publicPosts.label: Messages or suggestions shown publicly (nickname, text), for example a guestbook
f.collect_memory.label: A small cookie in the browser to remember a choice, for example a vote
f.collect_chat.label: Chat nicknames kept by a bot (Twitch commands)
f.collect_list.label: A list of e-mail addresses (newsletter) managed outside the site
f.collect_thirdParty.label: Content from another service shown in your pages (video player, widget…)
f.thirdPartyNames.label: Which services?
f.thirdPartyNames.help: Example: Twitch, YouTube. Needed if you ticked the box just above.
f.listTool.label: Tool that manages the e-mail list
f.listTool.help: Optional. The name of the mailing service you use.
f.unknownExt.label: Do the extensions I do not know collect information or set cookies?
f.otherCollect.label: Other information or cookies collected
f.otherCollect.help: One or two plain sentences. They will be used as written in your pages, in French and in English: write them in both languages if your site has two.
f.retention.label: Time after the last exchange
f.sells.label: Sales
f.sellsWhere.label: On which service?
f.sellsWhere.help: Example: the name of your online shop.
err.required: This field is needed to publish your pages.
err.choose: Pick an answer from the list.
err.email: Write a complete e-mail address, for example name@example.org.
err.name: Write a name of at least 2 letters, for example Jane Martin.
err.address: Write the full address with postcode and town, for example: 12 Lilac Street, 1000 Brussels.
err.phone: Write a number with its country code, for example +32 2 123 45 67.
err.hostAck: Tick this box only once you have given your identity to your host. Otherwise untick the previous box and write your address.
err.legalForm: Write the legal form, for example SRL, SAS or ASBL.
err.regNumber.BE: A Belgian company number has 10 digits, for example 0123.456.789.
err.regNumber.FR: A SIREN has 9 digits and a SIRET 14, for example 123 456 789 00012.
err.regNumber.CH: An IDE number starts with CHE, for example CHE-123.456.789.
err.regNumber.CA_QC: A NEQ has 10 digits, for example 1234567890.
err.regNumber.free: Write the number as it appears on your official documents, for example ABC-123.
err.vat: Write the number as it appears on your invoices, for example BE0123.456.789.
err.director: Write the name of the person in charge of publication, for example Jane Martin.
err.hostName: Write the name of the company that hosts your site, as on your invoice, for example “Host Ltd”.
err.hostAddress: Write the full address of your host (it is on its invoice or in its legal notice), for example: 1 Server Avenue, 75000 Paris.
err.hostCountry: Write the name of the country, for example Belgium.
err.thirdPartyNames: Write the name of the service(s), for example Twitch, YouTube.
err.listTool: Write the name of the tool, for example your mailing service.
err.otherCollect: Describe in one sentence what is collected, for example: “an anonymous click counter”.
err.sellsWhere: Write the name of the service where the sales happen, for example the name of your online shop.
err.step: This question does not exist. Go back to the wizard home.
err.ack: Tick the box to confirm that you have read your texts.
err.publishGap: A text was left incomplete: nothing was published. Open the preview to see what is missing.
public.index.title: Legal information
public.index.desc: Legal notice, privacy and cookies of this site.
public.index.intro: Here is the information that frames this site: who publishes it, what it does with your personal data and what it puts in your browser.
doc.notice.title: Legal notice
doc.notice.desc: Who publishes {site}, how to contact the publisher and who hosts the site.
doc.notice.editor.person: The site {site} is published in a personal capacity by {name}.
doc.notice.editor.self: The site {site} is published by {name}, who works as a self-employed person.
doc.notice.editor.association: The site {site} is published by the association {name}.
doc.notice.editor.company: The site {site} is published by the company {name}.
doc.notice.hidden: The publisher is a private individual. They chose not to make their full identity and address public: in accordance with article 6 of the French law no. 2004-575 of 21 June 2004 on confidence in the digital economy, they gave them to the host named below.
doc.notice.host.name: Name: {value}
doc.notice.sells.text: Purchases offered from this site are made on {where}, under the terms of that service.
doc.notice.ip.text: Unless stated otherwise, the texts, images, videos and logos of this site are protected by copyright. To reuse them, first ask {name} for permission at {email}. Third-party brands and logos belong to their owners.
doc.notice.links.text: This site links to other sites. Their content does not depend on {name}, who cannot be held responsible for it.
doc.privacy.title: Privacy
doc.privacy.desc: What personal information {site} collects, why, for how long, and how to exercise your rights.
doc.privacy.who: {name} is responsible for the personal information described on this page. For any question: {email}.
doc.privacy.who.CA_QC: {name} is the person in charge of the protection of personal information. For any question or request: {email}.
doc.privacy.technical: This page complements the [privacy policy of the site](@privacy), which describes how it works technically (cookies, visit statistics, features).
doc.privacy.c.nothing: This site does not ask you for any personal information: you can browse it without identifying yourself.
doc.privacy.c.messages: **If you write to us**: your name, e-mail address and message. We use them only to answer you.
doc.privacy.c.publicPosts: **If you leave a message, a suggestion or a vote**: your nickname (or first name) and your text are saved and may be shown publicly on this site.
doc.privacy.c.chat: **If you use a command in the chat**: your nickname and the command are kept in a short log that only the site team can read.
doc.privacy.c.memory: **If you make a choice, such as a vote**: a small cookie saved in your browser remembers it. It is used for nothing else.
doc.privacy.c.list: **If you subscribe to our newsletter**: your e-mail address is saved{tool} to send you the messages you asked for. You can unsubscribe at any time.
doc.privacy.c.thirdParty: **Content from other services**: some pages show content from {names}. By displaying it, you send your IP address to that service, which may also set its own cookies and applies its own privacy rules.
doc.privacy.c.host: Like any host, {host} may keep technical connection logs (including the IP address) to keep the server secure and running.
doc.privacy.basis.h: Why are we allowed to use it?
doc.privacy.basis.messages: Your messages: our legitimate interest in answering the people who write to us.
doc.privacy.basis.publicPosts: What you post: your choice to post it.
doc.privacy.basis.chat: The chat log: our legitimate interest in running and securing the commands.
doc.privacy.basis.list: The newsletter: your consent, which you can withdraw at any time.
doc.privacy.keep.h: How long do we keep it?
doc.privacy.keep.messages: Your messages are kept for {period} after our last exchange, then deleted.
doc.privacy.keep.publicPosts: What you post stays visible until you ask for it to be removed.
doc.privacy.keep.chat: The chat log keeps only the latest exchanges.
doc.privacy.keep.list: Your address stays on the list until you unsubscribe.
doc.privacy.share.never: Your information is neither sold nor given away.
doc.privacy.share.host: They are stored with the site's host, {host}.
doc.privacy.share.list: Your e-mail address is entrusted to {tool}, which manages the mailing list.
doc.privacy.share.thirdParty: The services {names} receive your IP address when you display their content.
doc.privacy.rights.BE: You can ask to access the information about you, to have it corrected or deleted, object to its use, and ask for it to be restricted or transferred (portability). Write to us at {email}: we answer within one month. If you believe your rights are not respected, you can lodge a complaint with the [Data Protection Authority]({authority}) (Belgium).
doc.privacy.rights.FR: You can ask to access the information about you, to have it corrected or deleted, object to its use, and ask for it to be restricted or transferred (portability). Write to us at {email}: we answer within one month. If you believe your rights are not respected, you can lodge a complaint with the [CNIL]({authority}) (France).
doc.privacy.rights.CH: You can ask to access the information about you, to have it corrected or deleted, and object to its use. Write to us at {email}: we answer within 30 days. You can also contact the [Federal Data Protection and Information Commissioner]({authority}) (Switzerland).
doc.privacy.rights.CA: You can ask to access the personal information we hold about you, have it corrected, and withdraw your consent. Write to us at {email}: we answer within 30 days. If you are not satisfied with our answer, you can complain to the [Office of the Privacy Commissioner of Canada]({authority}).
doc.privacy.rights.CA_QC: You can ask to access the personal information we hold about you, have it corrected, withdraw your consent, ask for its dissemination to stop, and ask to receive it in a structured, commonly used technological format. Write to the person in charge of the protection of personal information: {email}. We answer within 30 days. You can also contact the [Commission d'accès à l'information du Québec]({authority}).
doc.privacy.rights.OTHER: You can ask to access the information about you, to have it corrected or deleted. Write to us at {email}. Depending on the country where you live, you can also contact the authority in charge of personal data protection.
doc.cookies.title: Cookies
doc.cookies.desc: The cookies {site} puts in your browser, what they are for and how to refuse them.
doc.cookies.what.h: What this site puts in your browser
doc.cookies.none: This site sets no advertising cookie and no cookie that tracks your browsing, and it uses no audience measurement tool that sets any. That is why it does not ask you to accept cookies.
doc.cookies.noneExceptThirdParty: Apart from the content from other services described below, this site sets no advertising cookie and no cookie that tracks your browsing, and it uses no audience measurement tool that sets any.
doc.cookies.essential: A few working cookies may be saved, for example to remember the language you choose. They are needed for the service you ask for: they do not need your consent.
doc.cookies.memory: If you make a choice, such as a vote, a small cookie remembers it in your browser. It is used for nothing else.
doc.cookies.thirdParty: The content from {names} shown on some pages may set its own cookies. This site does not control them: see the policy of the service concerned.
doc.cookies.other: Other cookies or information reported by the publisher: {text}
doc.cookies.technical: The up-to-date list of the site's cookies is in the [privacy policy of the site](@privacy).
doc.cookies.manage.h: How to refuse or delete them
doc.cookies.manage.text: You can block or delete cookies at any time in your browser settings. Some features may then stop working (for example remembering your language).
doc.cookies.more.BE: The [Data Protection Authority]({authority}) explains the cookie rules in Belgium.
doc.cookies.more.FR: The [CNIL]({authority}) explains the cookie rules in France.
